sections.sectionSummaryBrief: Even though charity is given before prayer, it is merely a preparation for prayer and not the essential service of gemilus chassadim.

translations.translation: And even though even before prayer one must give gemilus chassadim,
as our sages said,
"One gives a coin to a poor person and then prays,"
nevertheless, the nature of this charity
is that it is a preparation for prayer,
and not the matter of the service of gemilus chassadim
(in its own right).
And certainly giving a coin is not a matter of "one who occupies himself with gemilus chassadim,"
the occupation with gemilus chassadim.
(And so too regarding the study of Torah,
for even though before prayer one recites the verses of "I will bless You" etc. — this study is not the occupation with Torah,
and the essence of "one who occupies himself with Torah" is specifically after prayer.)

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: One might explain the order in the Gemara based on the verse, but the verse itself still presents a difficulty in its sequence.

translations.translation: And seemingly it would be possible to explain,
that the reason for the order in the Gemara is due to the order in the verse.
For first it is stated "in peace" which is Torah and gemilus chassadim,
and afterwards — "for many were with me" which is the matter of communal prayer.
But still there is a difficulty in the order of the verse itself,
for seemingly it should say first "for many were with me" and afterwards "He redeemed my soul in peace."
And even though according to its simple meaning "for many were with me" is a reason for "He redeemed my soul in peace,"
and a verse does not depart from its simple meaning,
nevertheless we find in several verses
that they precede the reason for the matter to the matter itself.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: The difference between Torah and gemilus chassadim versus prayer is that the former draw down from above to below while the latter elevates from below to above, with prayer preceding to enable the drawing down.

translations.translation: And the explanation is,
that the entirety of man's service is in two ways: elevation from below to above and drawing down from above to below.
And this is the difference between Torah and gemilus chassadim and prayer,
that Torah and gemilus chassadim are a matter of drawing down from above to below, and prayer is a matter of elevation from below to above.
And the ultimate intention is to make for Him a dwelling place in the lower realms,
a drawing down from above to below through Torah and gemilus chassadim,
except that in order for Torah and gemilus chassadim to be as they should,
it is through the precedence of the elevation of prayer.
